proposed.sourceName: US FDA — 21 CFR §101.22(a)(3), definition of natural flavor
proposed.paraphrase: The US federal definition of 'natural flavor' permits derivation from 'meat, seafood, poultry, eggs, dairy products, or fermentation products thereof' as well as plant material, and the specific constituents need not be disclosed — so a bare 'natural flavors' declaration does not establish whether the source is halal.

proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation — Halal Certification for Natural & Artificial Flavors
proposed.paraphrase: The American Halal Foundation states natural flavors are not halal by default: flavors from haram animal sources or animal derivatives are haram, and ethanol-extracted flavors with residuals above 5000 ppm are haram; halal status requires verification of source and process.

researcherNote: Lenient position. Even under a permissive lens the source remains undisclosed/possibly non-halal, so the ingredient stays contested pending verification -> seeded draft grade 3 (Questionable - contested). Lenient requires two independent sources; FDA + AHF present. APPROVED by owner 2026-06-28.
